description: File import fixtures (Paket 11, Phase B; contract: docs/analyse/Paket11-PhaseB-Datei-IO-Vertrag.md, findings F1..F14: docs/analyse/Paket11-PhaseA-Datei-IO-Analyse.md). Every case is a real file: 'bytes' are hex bytes (separated by spaces, empty = 0 bytes) or 'generate' is a byte count of the deterministic ASCII text of 'generator' (written at test run time, never versioned). 'file' is the file name. Import paths: 'button' = OpenFileButton (real file chosen with DOM.setFileInputFiles, the Chromium file chooser path) and 'drop' = drag-and-drop onto the Remove textarea (real file dropped with Input.dispatchDragEvent). Before every case the target textarea holds 'previousText'. Expectations describe the CURRENT behaviour: { text } = the textarea state is exactly this text and no error message is shown, { generatedText: true } = the state is exactly the generated text, { unchanged: true } = 'previousText' stays and no message is shown, { rejected: invalidEncoding | tooLarge | unsupportedExtension } = 'previousText' stays and exactly one error message is shown (since C3 the localized message of that reason, the same for both paths; before C3 'message' named the exact English drop text). 'expected' applies to both paths; a case where the paths differ uses 'expectedButton' + 'expectedDrop'. 'target' is the decided behaviour of the contract (both paths; a rejected target names no message text, the wording is open), always with 'pending' { decisions, phase, paths, reason }: exactly the paths listed in 'paths' still differ from the target (checked against the real app by the integration tests and for consistency by tests/unit/file-io-fixtures.test.ts). A case without 'target' already meets the contract. 'ref' is a Phase A finding, 'note' explains a case, 'resolved' explains an expectation changed by a correction (Paket 11 C1: D1, empty content; C3: D3-D8, strict decoding, 10 MiB and .txt for both paths).

generator.note: The generated text is 'line' repeated and cut to the byte count (ASCII only, so bytes = UTF-16 code units).

cases.name: empty file (0 bytes)
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C1 (D1): the button ignored an empty content (if (content)); it now sets every content read successfully, also ''.

cases.name: UTF-8 BOM only
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C1 (D1): the BOM is removed and the content '' now replaces the text (the button ignored it before).

cases.name: UTF-16LE BOM only
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C1 (D1): as the UTF-8 BOM, the decoded content '' now replaces the text (the button ignored it before).

cases.name: UTF-16BE BOM only
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C1 (D1): as the UTF-8 BOM, the decoded content '' now replaces the text (the button ignored it before).

cases.name: UTF-8 with BOM: the BOM is removed
cases.bytes: EF BB BF 47 72 C3 BC C3 9F 65

cases.name: UTF-8 with two BOMs: only the first one is the signature
cases.bytes: EF BB BF EF BB BF 61
cases.note: The second U+FEFF is content (ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE) and is kept.

cases.name: invalid UTF-8 byte
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C3 (D5): the case now meets the contract (both paths). Before C3 the result was text "a�b"; reason: readAsText replaces invalid bytes with U+FFFD without a message.

cases.name: truncated UTF-8 sequence at the end
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C3 (D5): the case now meets the contract (both paths). Before C3 the result was text "a�"; reason: the incomplete 4-byte sequence becomes one U+FFFD.

cases.name: Windows-1252 umlauts (not UTF-8)
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C3 (D5, D6): the case now meets the contract (both paths). Before C3 the result was text "Gr��e"; reason: no encoding detection (D6): the bytes are invalid UTF-8 and must be refused instead of damaged.

cases.name: encoded surrogate (CESU-8)
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C3 (D5): the case now meets the contract (both paths). Before C3 the result was text "���"; reason: uTF-8 must not encode surrogates; every byte becomes U+FFFD.

cases.name: overlong UTF-8 encoding
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C3 (D5): the case now meets the contract (both paths). Before C3 the result was text "��"; reason: overlong '/' is invalid UTF-8.

cases.name: UTF-16LE without BOM, non-ASCII (invalid UTF-8)
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C3 (D5, D6): the case now meets the contract (both paths). Before C3 the result was text "H\u0000�\u0000"; reason: without a BOM the file is read as UTF-8 (D6: no detection); E4 00 is invalid UTF-8.

cases.name: UTF-16LE without BOM, ASCII only (valid UTF-8 with NUL)
cases.note: D6: no encoding detection. The bytes are valid UTF-8 (NUL is a valid character), so the contract keeps this result.

cases.name: UTF-16LE with BOM and a lone surrogate
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C3 (D4, D5): the case now meets the contract (both paths). Before C3 the result was text "�A"; reason: an unpaired high surrogate is an invalid UTF-16 sequence and becomes U+FFFD.

cases.name: UTF-16LE with BOM and an odd byte count
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C3 (D4, D5): the case now meets the contract (both paths). Before C3 the result was text "A"; reason: the last single byte is an incomplete code unit; today it is dropped without a message. Chromium's FileReader.readAsText silently drops the incomplete last code unit (the WHATWG decode gives U+FFFD; Chromium's TextDecoder does so too and throws with fatal: true). Silent data loss, found in Phase B.

cases.name: valid U+FFFD inside the text
cases.note: Added in C3: a correctly encoded U+FFFD is content; only invalid bytes are refused (no search for U+FFFD).

cases.name: UTF-16BE with BOM and an odd byte count
cases.note: Added in C3 (D4, D5): the incomplete last code unit is refused, not dropped.

cases.name: UTF-16BE with BOM and a lone surrogate
cases.note: Added in C3 (D4, D5): an unpaired high surrogate in UTF-16BE is refused.

cases.name: U+2028 and U+2029 inside a line
exactly 10 MiB
cases.note: D7: the limit is inclusive. The drop limit is `file.size > maxSize`, so exactly 10 MiB is already allowed.

cases.name: 10 MiB + 1 byte
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C3 (D7): the case now meets the contract (both paths). Before C3 the result was button: the generated text, drop: rejected (tooLarge); reason: openFileButton has no size limit.

cases.name: upper-case extension .TXT
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C3 (D8): the case now meets the contract (both paths). Before C3 the result was button: text "upper", drop: rejected (unsupportedExtension); reason: the drop checks file.name.endsWith('.txt') case-sensitively.

cases.name: mixed-case extension .Txt
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C3 (D8): the case now meets the contract (both paths). Before C3 the result was button: text "mixed", drop: rejected (unsupportedExtension); reason: the drop checks file.name.endsWith('.txt') case-sensitively.

cases.name: other extension .csv
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C3 (D8): the case now meets the contract (both paths). Before C3 the result was button: text "a,b", drop: rejected (unsupportedExtension); reason: accept=".txt" only preselects the dialog filter; a file chosen with another extension ("All files") is read.

cases.name: no extension
cases.resolved: Paket 11 C3 (D8): the case now meets the contract (both paths). Before C3 the result was button: text "readme", drop: rejected (unsupportedExtension); reason: openFileButton does not check the extension.

scenarioDescription: Import flows of the integration tests (checkFileIo in tests/e2e/lib/app.mjs, same names). 'current' and 'target' are the observations of the flow; 'pending' { decisions, phase, fields, reason } lists exactly the fields where 'current' still differs from 'target' (none = the flow already meets the contract); 'resolved' explains an observation changed by a correction. 'method': 'real' = real file chooser path / real drop and real reads, 'gated' = real reads whose START is held and released by the test in a fixed order (controlled race simulation, FileReader and Blob read methods wrapped in the page), 'intercepted' = the file chooser is opened with a user gesture and intercepted by CDP (no native dialog). 'readOnly' is the readOnly attribute of the target textarea, 'busy' its aria-busy="true" (D11; since C2 together with the visible hint notifications.fileLoading next to the Open File button). 'note' explains a field or flow added later.

scenarios.name: same file chosen again
scenarios.steps: Choose A (FILE_A + CRLF) on Split, edit the text, choose A again, change A on disk and choose it again, choose B then A, leave the page and come back, choose A again.
scenarios.resolved: Paket 11 C2 (D2): the input kept its value, Chromium fired no change for the same path (againAfterEdit and againAfterDiskChange stayed 'EDITED'); OpenFileButton now resets the value after taking the file.

scenarios.name: read error on the button
scenarios.steps: A path that does not exist is chosen on Split (real change event, the FileReader fails with NotFoundError); then a file is created at that path and the same path is chosen again.
scenarios.resolved: Paket 11 C1 (D13): useSnackbar() was called inside reader.onerror ('Invalid hook call', production: Minified React error #321, no message); it is now called by the component and the error shows notifications.readError. 'retryLoads' was added in C2 (D2: a new choice of the same path after an error; before C2 it fired no change).

scenarios.name: read error on the drop
scenarios.steps: A path that does not exist is dropped onto the Remove textarea.

scenarios.name: loading state of the shared target
scenarios.steps: Choose a file on Split and hold its read; check the textarea and the loading hint, select and copy text (copy command with a user gesture), type with real key input, check the file input; release.
scenarios.resolved: Paket 11 C2 (D10, D11): there was no loading state (editable, not busy, typed text replaced by the file later); the target textarea is now readOnly with aria-busy and the hint notifications.fileLoading while its import runs. 'hint', 'copied' and 'hintAfter' were added in C2.

scenarios.name: newer file replaces a running import
scenarios.steps: Choose A, then B on Split (both reads held); release B, then A.
scenarios.resolved: Paket 11 C2 (D9, D12): every FileReader set the text when it finished, the older A overwrote B; now only the latest import of the target sets the text.

scenarios.name: older import finishes first
scenarios.steps: Choose A, then B on Split (both held); release A first, then B.
scenarios.note: Added in C2 (D9): the replaced A neither sets its text nor ends the loading state of B.

scenarios.name: replaced import fails late
scenarios.steps: Choose A, then B on Split (both held); release B; delete A on disk; release A (real NotFoundError).
scenarios.resolved: Paket 11 C1 (D13): the late error threw the hook error (F1) and showed no message; after C1 it showed the read error message. Paket 11 C2 (D9): a replaced import is ignored silently.

scenarios.name: refused choice during a running import
scenarios.steps: Choose A on Split (read held), then choose a .csv file with the button; release A.
scenarios.note: Added in C3 (D8, decision of the C3 task): a refused file is no import job; it shows exactly the message of its reason, A stays the current import, sets its text and ends the lock.

scenarios.name: newer import fails to decode
scenarios.steps: Choose A on Split, then B with invalid UTF-8 bytes (both held); release B, then A; then choose a valid file.
scenarios.note: Added in C3 (D5, D9): an accepted file that fails to decode is a started import; it replaces A, keeps the text, shows the invalid encoding message and ends the lock; the late A is ignored; a new import works.

scenarios.name: refused drop during a running import
scenarios.steps: Choose A with the button on Remove (read held), then drop a file of 10 MiB + 1 byte; release A.
scenarios.note: Added in C3 (D7, decision of the C3 task): the same rule for the drop; the too large file is refused before reading and A stays the current import.

scenarios.name: button and drop share the Remove target
scenarios.steps: Choose A with the button, then drop B onto the Remove textarea (both held); release B, then A.
scenarios.resolved: Paket 11 C2 (D9, D10): button and drop read independently and A overwrote B; both are now imports of the shared source text (one job sequence, one lock).

scenarios.name: drop then button on the Remove target
scenarios.steps: Drop A onto the Remove textarea, then choose B with the button (both held); release B; delete A on disk; release A (real NotFoundError).
scenarios.note: Added in C2 (D9, D12): the reverse order of the shared Remove target; the late error of the replaced drop shows no message.

scenarios.name: independent Diff targets
scenarios.steps: Hold an import into the old Diff text, then one into the new Diff text; release both.
scenarios.resolved: Paket 11 C2 (D10): there was no lock; now each Diff text is locked only by its own import (the old text is the shared source text, the new text a page-local target).

scenarios.name: navigation during an import into the shared text
scenarios.steps: Hold an import on Split, go to Sort, check the Sort textarea, release.
scenarios.resolved: Paket 11 C2 (D10): the import state of the shared text lives in PageList next to sourceText, so the lock follows the text to the next page.

scenarios.name: navigation during an import into the new Diff text
scenarios.steps: Hold an import into the new Diff text, go to Split, release; then go back to Diff. Again with a file deleted before its read: no message after the page is gone.
scenarios.note: 'lateErrorMessage' was added in C2: the import of the unmounted page is disposed (before C2 its error still showed the message of the unmounted button).

scenarios.name: cancelled file dialog
scenarios.steps: Choose A on Split, edit the text, open the file chooser with a user gesture and close it without a file (no change; the cancel event Chromium fires is dispatched by the test), then choose A again.
scenarios.resolved: Paket 11 C2 (D2, D14): after a cancel the input still held A and choosing A again fired no change; the value is now reset after every choice. 'readOnlyWhileOpen' was added in C2: opening the dialog sets no lock.
